content: A total of 25 records were identified and downloaded during a search for terms related to medicine, medication, prescriptions, generics, vaccines, biosimilars, and similar biologics. In another search, 119 records were retrieved using terms related to cost-plus pricing in the context of pharmaceuticals. A subsequent search for terms like price threshold, price cap, and price ceiling yielded 213 records. When searching for pricing and mark-up in relation to drugs and pharmaceuticals, 426 records were identified. Searching for price transparency and related terms in the context of pharmaceuticals yielded 170 records. Another search focusing on discount transparency and related terms retrieved 42 records. Searching for rebate transparency and similar terms yielded 8 records. A search for managed entry and risk-sharing schemes in the context of drug pricing identified 99 records. Searching for terms like access with evidence development and conditional coverage yielded 49 records. A search for pooled procurement in the pharmaceutical context identified 538 records, but due to system limitations, only 500 records could be downloaded. Additional searches were conducted on various websites and databases. For example, a search on a specific webpage on September 24, 2019, retrieved 2 records, which were screened and imported into EndNote. Another search on September 26, 2019, retrieved 58 records, which were similarly screened and imported. A search on September 23, 2019, retrieved 136 records, which were screened for eligibility, resulting in 136 potentially relevant results. In another search conducted on September 24, 2019, 17 records were retrieved and screened, all of which were downloaded. A search on September 27, 2019, retrieved 3,075 records, which were screened to exclude duplicates and irrelevant results. After deduplication, 1,027 records were loaded into an EndNote library, and further screening reduced the number to 567 relevant records. Reference checking was also performed, with records retrieved from sources like the Web of Science. For example, a study on the impact of generic substitution on price competition in Finland listed 15 references, 11 of which were retrieved. Other studies focused on topics such as orphan drug policies, pharmaceutical pricing in developing countries, and the effects of pricing policies on drug expenditures. The searches and analyses covered a wide range of topics, including the impact of generic entry on pricing, centralized procurement strategies, biosimilar competition, and the effects of price regulation on healthcare expenditures. These efforts aimed to gather comprehensive data on pharmaceutical pricing policies and their implications across different countries and healthcare systems.
